title: Private vs. shareable info
intro: Some information is fun to share online, like your favourite colour or a drawing you made.
Other information is private, because it helps strangers find you or get into your accounts: your address, school, phone number, passwords and photos that show where you are.
Before you send something, ask: does this help someone know who I am and where I am? If so, it's private. When you're not sure, ask a grown-up.

game.prompt: What's private, and what's OK to share in a game or chat?

items.explain: An address tells strangers exactly where you live.
A favourite colour doesn't help anyone find you. Fun to share!
Your school tells people where you are almost every day.

items.text: A drawing of a dragon you made
items.explain: A drawing is a great way to share without giving away details.
A password is never shared, except with your parents.

items.text: What you thought of a book you read
items.explain: Opinions and hobbies are fine to share. Just don't add details like your full name or address.

items.text: A photo of you wearing your school logo
items.explain: Photos can give away where you are too. Check what shows in the background and on your clothes.

quiz.question: Which of these is private?
quiz.explain: A phone number lets strangers contact you, so it stays private.

quiz.question: You want to send a photo. What do you check first?
options: That it shows no address, street sign or school logo
That it has at least three people in it
quiz.explain: Little details in the background can show where you are.

quiz.question: You're not sure if something is private. What do you do?
options: Ask a parent or another adult you trust
quiz.explain: When you're not sure, stop and ask. Better to ask than be sorry.

summary: Private information like your address, school, phone number and passwords stays with you. Hobbies, opinions and drawings are fine to share. When unsure, ask a grown-up.
